headline: Braves take Game 1, Phillies face elimination in Game 2
recap: The Phillies opened the postseason with a 5-3 loss to the Braves in Game 1 of the NL Wild Card Series at Truist Park. Alec Bohm's double in the top of the first drove in Kyle Schwarber for an early 1-0 lead, but Mike Yastrzemski's RBI single tied it in the bottom half. Ozzie Albies' triple scored Michael Harris II in the sixth to put Atlanta ahead 2-1, and Philadelphia answered in the seventh when J.T. Realmuto's triple brought home both Bryan De La Cruz and Bryson Stott for a 3-2 lead. Austin Riley erased that lead for good in the eighth with a three-run homer off Jhoan Duran. Jesus Luzardo started for the Phillies and allowed one earned run over five innings with six strikeouts; Duran took the loss in relief. Chris Sale started for Atlanta and struck out nine over 6 1/3 innings, Dylan Lee picked up the win, and Raisel Iglesias closed it out for the save.

The loss puts Philadelphia down 0-1 in the best-of-three series, one defeat from elimination. The Phillies finished the regular season 88-74, second in the NL East, six games behind Atlanta's division-winning 94-68 mark, before claiming the National League's final wild card spot.

The series shifts to Game 2 today at Truist Park, first pitch 2:00 p.m. ET. Cristopher Sanchez starts for Philadelphia against Atlanta's Tyler Mahle. A Phillies win forces a decisive Game 3 tomorrow; a loss ends their season. DraftKings has Philadelphia as a narrow moneyline favorite at -114, with Atlanta at -106.
